findings.title: Accepted POI with absent explicit type cannot be relocated
requirements: M02: if explicit type is absent, preserve absence without inventing a new random type
reproduction: Create regionFixture() accepted v7 map; remove map.regions[0].pointOfInterestKinds while leaving pointsOfInterest=[{q:2,r:0}]. This is valid under existing save schema and displays as a generic point.
Import with actual handleImportJson: accepted, no alert; enter Edit; startPoiDraft land region1 2,0 succeeds.
Choose existing empty land target 3,0. Actual App VM reports poi_kind_mismatch; real production DOM disables Done and displays 'Тип точки несовместим с назначением. (; 3,0)'.
findings.actual: The !kind guard treats supported absence as incompatible unknown type. Neither within-region nor cross-region relocation can proceed. Unknown explicit legacy type is a different case already intentionally refused.
findings.expected: Preserve a valid untyped point's missing pointOfInterestKinds entry through relocation and one reversible transaction, without generating a type. Retain explicit unknown/incompatible type refusal. If analyst intended missing type to be forbidden, resolve the M02 conflict explicitly rather than claiming full AC acceptance.
findings.suggested_verification: Extend existing no-op/type compatibility and real move cases with accepted missing-kind input; verify absence at new address, no invented value and exact Undo/Redo.

findings.title: v8 authored name accepts a locator shared by central and ordinary POI
requirements: E8 naming: validator checks exactly one addressee
Format/compatibility: invalid/dangling/colliding address is atomic refusal
reproduction: Take regionFixture(); set version8; enable center0,0 centralPoiKind='lair', suppressCentralPoi=false; append ordinary point {q:0,r:0} with pointOfInterestKinds['0,0']='ruins'.
Import through real handleImportJson. It succeeds with no alert and exports the same ambiguous name.
findings.actual: poiNameLocators inserts both distinct live objects into a Set under the same address. assertPoiEditorNames checks only Set membership and cannot detect multiple addressees. The ambiguous name becomes accepted document state and catalog identity.
findings.expected: Refuse the authored-name address at map.editorNames before document/history/RNG changes, or prevent naming this ambiguous address while preserving ability to inspect legacy map data. Do not arbitrarily choose central/ordinary object or silently prune payload.
findings.suggested_verification: Extend existing malformed/orphan import case with central+ordinary shared locator and verify accepted document plus both histories unchanged; also verify authoring on ambiguous old maps cannot bypass the same check.

findings.title: Renaming a kingdom bypasses collision checks against new authored POI names
requirements: E8 common-name uniqueness across live names and kingdom names per language
reproduction: Import Mythic regionFixture with ordinary monument2,0.
Use real pair editor callbacks to author POI RU='Моё имя', EN='My Name'; save succeeds.
Open kingdom:1 and rename RU to 'Моё имя'. saveNameDraft returns true and exports both kingdom and POI with identical RU.
findings.actual: New POI rename checks kingdom names, but reverse kingdom rename deliberately skips all duplicate checks (current.type !== 'kingdom'). New editorNames interaction therefore has asymmetric uniqueness.
findings.expected: Apply the agreed per-language collision policy consistently for the new layer while excluding the same entity, retaining old duplicate compatibility/no-op semantics.
findings.scope_caution: The kingdom exemption predates E8; this finding concerns incomplete integration of new editorNames into the E8 uniqueness contract, not a claim that E8 introduced the pre-existing kingdom-only duplicate policy.
findings.suggested_verification: Extend existing cross-registry duplicate name case to test both edit directions and same-entity/fallback exclusions.
